messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] SEV2 - GPU pool us-west-2/gpu-pool-01 saturated. queue_length=4210, pending_requests=3800, avg_token_latency=1.9s, tail_latency=6.3s. autoscaler: scale_up_failures=7, last_error=\"scale_up_timeout after 300s\". dashboard: https://redwood.ops/d/cluster/gpu-pool-01

oncall-aaron: ack. paging sre-jen and ml-ops-ankita. taking first response. @sre-jen @ml-ops-ankita can you confirm impact surface? :loud_sound:

sre-jen: looking. seeing continuous-batcher backlog growth across gpus. prefix cache hit rate dropped from 88% -> 34% in last 12m. lots of cache-miss amplification. autoscaler attempted to add nodes but hit AWS ASG scale limit + AZ capacity errors.

ml-ops-ankita: customer-facing note: some high-traffic customers reported timeouts and 429s. CS already got a ticket from @cs-lee with org-id org_42.

cs-lee: confirming — multiple customers in org_42 saw 5xx and throttles, some on dedicated pools but routed to hosted fallback which is also noisy. collecting affected request IDs.

runtime-simon: quick hypothesis: recent change to continuous-batching params + a small prefix-cache eviction bug from last deploy (PR #4123) caused cold-prefix misses to hammer GPU memory and reduce batching efficiency. reduced effective throughput -> queue growth -> autoscaler flapping.

oncall-aaron: timeline: root alert at 1763280400. going to attempt mitigation: 1) disable continuous batching for models in the affected pool 2) increase prefix_cache.size temporarily 3) force-add warm nodes (if ASG permits) 4) route non-critical traffic to smaller model variant. executing now.

sre-jen: running quick config patch to disable continuous batching for pool tag=us-west-2/gpu-pool-01. command:
```bash
# patch the batcher config in runtime-config k8s configmap
kubectl -n infra patch configmap runtime-batcher -p '{"data":{"continuous_batching_enabled":"false"}}' || true
```

infra-bot: deploy-bot triggered: runtime-config updated (continuous_batching_enabled=false) by sre-jen. diff: -true +false. rollout started to batcher pods (5/5). logs: batcher-1 restarting.

runtime-simon: good. also bumping prefix cache size to reduce thrash. applying runtime tweak:
```json
{"prefix_cache": {"max_entries": 250000, "eviction_policy": "lru"}}
```
patching via redwoodctl:
```bash
redwoodctl config set --pool us-west-2/gpu-pool-01 prefix_cache.max_entries=250000
```

platform-dana: trying to request more nodes via AWS. ASG hit account-level target, opening request with infra team. if that stalls we'll force-route non-critical jobs to us-east or fallback small models.

ml-ops-ankita: starting reroute rule: route tag=non-prod or customer_tier=free -> model:fast-small-v1 (lower memory). patching routing rules:
```yaml
- match:
    - customer_tier: free
    - tag: non-prod
  route_to: model: fast-small-v1
  priority: 20
```
applied.

oncall-aaron: so far after disabling continuous batching and bumping prefix cache: queue_length down from 4210 -> 980 in 6m. pending_requests from 3800 -> 870. tail latency trending down. still seeing some autoscaler errors for scale_up_timeout.

sre-jen: autoscaler logs show repeated errors: 
```
ERROR: failed to launch instance: InsufficientInstanceCapacity: We currently do not have enough capacity in the Availability Zone you requested.
  at autoscaler/scale.go:312
```
we're rebalancing to other AZs via ASG config change. Also raised ASG desired capacity manually as a short-term measure:
```bash
aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name gpu-asg-usw2-01 --desired-capacity 18 --honor-cooldown
```

infra-bot: ASG desired update accepted. requested 18, current 12. new instances provisioning. monitor EC2 init logs.

ml-ops-ankita: customer impact update: impacted requests mostly from high-concurrency generative endpoints (chat streaming). A few enterprise customers had transient failures, CS notified. we should prepare an incident notice with ETA for full recovery and root cause (probable config regression).

cs-lee: sending initial customer message: \"We're investigating elevated latencies and throttles affecting generation endpoints in US-WEST. We've applied mitigations and will provide updates every 30 minutes.\"

runtime-simon: note for postmortem: PR #4123 changed continuous_batching.default_max_latency from 50ms -> 250ms and introduced a bug where prefix cache keys were occasionally truncated (off-by-1), leading to massive cache miss amplification for common prefixes.

oncall-aaron: handoff: I'm handing to @sre-jen for next 3h to monitor recovery and run follow-ups. I'll remain on standby for exec questions. @sre-jen please confirm you accept.

sre-jen: accepted. will own until 1763289800. ongoing checks: verify prefix cache hit rate returns >80% and queue_length <200 across pools.

ml-ops-ankita: action items for post-incident: 1) revert PR #4123 change to continuous-batching defaults 2) patch prefix key generation bug and add unit tests 3) add ASG capacity alerts and cross-AZ fallback policy 4) run chaos test to ensure autoscaler handles sustained queue growth.

oncall-aaron: quick mitigation summary for timeline and customer comms:
- 1763280400: alert triggered (queue growth + autoscaler failures)
- 1763280460: disabled continuous batching (reduced batching latency)
- 1763280580: bumped prefix_cache.max_entries to 250k
- 1763280700: applied routing to fast-small-v1 for non-critical traffic
- 1763281000: ASG desired capacity increased, new nodes provisioning
- 1763282200: queue length stabilized ~ <150, tail latency improving

cs-lee: posting update to affected customers now. will include the above mitigation steps and ETA for postmortem.

infra-bot: monitoring: EC2 instances healthy=4 new, 8 starting, 6 in-service total now 16/18 desired. keep watching.
